name: Michal
overview: Michal, daughter of King Saul, was given to David as a reward for his victory over the Philistine giant Goliath, a union arranged through a challenging bride-price of two hundred Philistine foreskins (1 Samuel 18:25-27). This marriage not only signified David's rising favor in Saul’s court but also marked a complex relationship, as Saul later forcibly separated them and gave Michal to another man. The narrative highlights both the political and personal dimensions of Michal's role in David's life, reflecting the intertwining of divine providence and human agency in the unfolding of God's purposes.
